mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE increases > 0.3pp for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings for industrial firms and drags the S&P 500 lower over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% in the same month signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with cooling inflation, which increases risk-free rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) above their respective 6-month moving averages signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month moving averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for at least two consecutive quarters signals deep labor market distress, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which weakens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.
